Authority: reviewed kind:file tools accept only private uploads/private references tied to a caller-readable row; exact row access and uploader ownership are checked before byte reads. File tool grants require both files:read and the exact bound table's read scope.

file_ref: the file_ref may be the reference exactly as the row stores it: a logical uploads/private/... path, or, when the app's uploads go to the platform media CDN, the private CDN URL /api/_upload returned (https://<media CDN host>/private/<this app>/uploads/private/...), which is normalized to the logical path by the delete_upload rule and must be exactly that URL; another app's prefix, the public tier, another host or port, userinfo, a query or fragment, percent-encoding, dot segments and doubled slashes are invalid_input.

file_column: optional handler.file_column binds ingest/verify to one existing canonical readable text column (for example documents.file_url), included in reviewed digests. Initial read, cache reuse, snapshot transaction and result release recheck that exact current column, row authority and upload ownership; other text fields cannot vouch for it. Hidden, encrypted or non-text columns refuse. Without file_column a tool matches the reference against any string column of the row, which is not an exact version binding.

membership_constraints: optional handler.membership_constraints (for example {kind: human, status: active}) adds type-exact equalities on at most eight canonical groups columns to existing file authority. Values are strings of at most 128 bytes without NUL, booleans, or finite numbers with absolute value at most 1e15. Exactly one live canonical membership row must identify the actor in the selected tenant and satisfy every equality; duplicate rows cannot combine authority. Configured groups.table/key/user_field and declared readable columns are required; encryption configuration is optional, and encrypted, hidden and blind-index columns are refused. Current membership is rechecked on reads, cached results, verification, status and publication. `benmore mcp review`, `mcp check`/`inspect` and the push write gate refuse the manifest when the app has no configured groups.table/key/user_field (`tool "<name>" membership_constraints require configured groups.table, groups.key, and groups.user_field`), when the schema files do not declare the groups table with its key and user columns, or when a constrained column is not a readable, unencrypted column of that table. An app already running such a manifest keeps its connector and its other tools: the load log names the tool and every call to it answers denied.

upload_tenant: optional handler.upload_tenant: current requires an exact file_column (otherwise review refuses `upload_tenant must be current on a file handler with file_column`) and configured groups table/key/user_field plus that key on the source row. It requires the canonical private-upload owner record to have a nonempty group matching both the grant tenant and current source-row group, including on cached snapshot reuse, verify, status, snapshot transaction and final release. A handler that declares it cannot consume snapshots made without it; omitting the field keeps the admin/uploader/row-owner vouch policy. `benmore mcp inspect --json` shows the field as upload_tenant in the tool's handler. Review, check, inspect and the push write gate refuse the manifest without that groups configuration (`tool "<name>" upload_tenant requires current, a file_column, and configured groups.table/key/user_field`) or when the schema files do not declare the group key on the source table and the groups table. An app already running such a manifest keeps its connector and its other tools: the load log names the tool and every call to it answers denied.

status operation: a reviewed file handler `operation: status` requires string processing_id, record_id and file_ref inputs and returns bounded metadata only for a known successful snapshot-backed result under current authority. It exposes no parsed blocks or snapshot payload, and historical complete does not attest that current file bytes still match.

Tabular files: CSV, XLSX and XLSM are limited to 25 MiB and 100,000 cells, preserve sheet/cell coordinates, never truncate, record hashes/parser/limits/completion, and return bounded pages of 50 blocks (maximum 100).

Office documents: DOCX/PPTX use the bounded `doc-ooxml-text/1` parser: DOCX paragraphs/tables and PPTX presentation-order slides, notes and tables are text-only; layout and embedded visual content are not reconstructed, and tracked changes, alternate content or external text stories fail closed. `complete` covers the declared supported text scope, not rendered-document understanding.

PDF: native text is extracted with its layout, and only pages with no native text blocks fall back to OCR (English), page by page; mixed pages may omit raster-only text and carry the native_text_only_pages quality flag. Blocks have page, bbox and coordinate units; OCR blocks carry confidence plus quality flag ocr, never asserted as truth. PDF MIME and magic must match; encrypted PDFs fail (incomplete_result). Caps are 200 pages, 40,000,000 decoded pixels per page, 60s/512 MiB per page, 512 MiB total temporary bytes, and 10 minutes total. PDF extraction answers unavailable_provider when the host does not provide the PDF and OCR tools with English language data or cannot sandbox them.

Snapshots: successful ingest atomically stores immutable original bytes and full extracted blocks in a private snapshot in the app's database, bound to owner account incarnation, tenant, source table, record and file reference (an app without groups binds the empty tenant its grants carry; an app with groups never stores an empty or "0" tenant). It returns an opaque 32-character processing_id in the framework envelope, metadata and text, without changing reviewed data projections. Identical source bytes, owner binding, parser and limits reuse a verified snapshot; changed identity creates a new processing. Existing immutable processing IDs retain original extracted bytes but never grant current row/column access. Snapshots are capped at 128 MiB each and 1 GiB per app, and the plan's database storage limit also applies.

verify: verify requires that explicit processing_id and checks retained sheet/ref/value spans after current record/file authorization; it never reparses a replaced upload. A processing_id that has no stored snapshot cannot be verified.
Concurrency: each app process runs one file ingest or verify call at a time; other calls wait for it while their request lasts.
